editorNote: A two-story day, both about rates: a hawkish Fed repricing pushed gold to its worst week in months, while bitcoin extended a slide that has taken it to levels last seen in the summer.

stories.headline: Bitcoin falls about 8% after Friday's U.S. close to a three-month low just above $62,000
stories.summary: CoinDesk says bitcoin is down about 17% on the week and ether about 22%, with $62,500 back at the range lows from earlier this year. Analyst James Check called it the fourth capitulation event since the all-time high and a 'deep value' zone, while adding it doesn't mean the bottom is in; Bloomberg put the Sunday low at $62,022, the weakest since July 14.
stories.whyItMatters: BTC has now given back its late-summer rally, and the fall came as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to roughly 5.15%.

stories.headline: Gold ends a steep weekly loss near $3,880 as rate-hike bets and a 5.15% 10-year yield weigh
stories.summary: Per Reuters via CNBC, gold fell more than 4% on the week, its worst since early June, after a hot CPI print and a roughly 3% drop Thursday to a more than one-year low. Kitco had spot near $3,883 late Friday; October PPI rose 0.3% (0.4% expected), and futures priced about an 89% chance of a 25-basis-point Fed hike on Dec. 8-9.
stories.whyItMatters: Markets are pricing a Fed rate increase rather than a cut, which raises the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.
